human_understanding_delta: FormACutQuantitativeExpansion carries an anchored nonlinear remainder of size O(eta^2 |z|) and budgets it against the active margin. In the reciprocal power-sum coordinates p_m = sum_j a_j^-m that remainder is not an error: -p_m/m = E_m - ((m+1)/2) E_m^(2) + ..., so the quadratic correction is the second term of an exact coefficient. The expansion log|f(z)| = log|f(0)| - Re sum_m (p_m/m) z^m is a Taylor series, controlled in C^2 rather than C^0, so the unmodelled part can be pushed past any prescribed finite contact order. Newton's identity for the reversed polynomial makes every coefficient rational in the coefficients of f with denominator a power of f(0), so the normalisation is semialgebraic without a root labelling. Separately: the equal-radius staple length is exactly |a_i|+|a_j|-s(2-|u_i-u_j|), so moving root directions cost nothing in the length budget, and a zero-margin contact is decided by the completed-square discriminant V+eps+B^2/(4 kappa)<0, not by uniform convergence, whose countermodel is -x^2+eps.
